title: videoio: FFmpeg 9 compatibility for AVCodec::supported_framerates
body:
Description
While working on the remaining FFmpeg 9 compatibility changes, I found another direct access to AVCodec::supported_framerates in modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp.
The corresponding FFmpeg API is now:
avcodec_get_supported_config(
    NULL,
    codec,
    AV_CODEC_CONFIG_FRAME_RATE,
    0,
    (const void **)&supported_framerates,
    &num_supported_framerates);
Unlike the previous API, avcodec_get_supported_config() returns both the configuration pointer and the number of supported entries.
The current OpenCV implementation iterates using the sentinel-terminated array:
for (; p->den != 0; p++) {
    ...
}
Before preparing a PR, I'd like to clarify the preferred migration approach.
Should the implementation:

preserve the existing sentinel-based iteration (minimal compatibility change), or
iterate using the returned num_supported_framerates, following the newer FFmpeg API?

Note: The variable name num_supported_framerates in the example above is only used for illustration. The FFmpeg API itself exposes a generic out_num_configs parameter for all configuration types (PIX_FORMAT, FRAME_RATE, SAMPLE_RATE, SAMPLE_FORMAT, CHANNEL_LAYOUT, etc.), and the example simply shows its usage for the frame-rate configuration.
the above mentioned code is just for understanding
I'd be happy to prepare a PR based on the preferred approach.

Detailed description
The crash is a heap out-of-bounds write (4 bytes, one past the end) in cv::generateDescriptorSubsample at AKAZEFeatures.cpp:2625. ASan reports the write lands 0 bytes after a 256-byte region allocated at AKAZEFeatures.cpp:2591 — the comps matrix sized nchannels * npicks. With nchannels=2 the code writes 3 entries per pick (the +0/+1/+2 block), and the last pick's +2 write overflows the buffer. The second stack trace confirms the allocation originated in generateDescriptorSubsample, tying the overflow directly to the library.
PoC legitimacy per API documentation

API entry point: cv::Ptr<AKAZE> cv::AKAZE::create() (OpenCV features2d API).
descriptor_type = DESCRIPTOR_MLDB: documented enum value; selects the MLDB descriptor path that calls generateDescriptorSubsample. The crash report confirms any descriptor type ≥ DESCRIPTOR_MLDB_UPRIGHT reaches this code.
descriptor_size = 32: docs state "Size of the descriptor in bits. 0 means full size; other values are clipped to the nearest multiple of 8." 32 is valid, and any non-zero value triggers the subsampling path.
descriptor_channels = 2: docs state "The number of channels in the descriptor (1, 2, 3)." 2 is explicitly permitted. The buggy function's own docstring (AKAZEFeatures.cpp:2550) repeats: @param nchannels Number of channels to consider in the descriptor (1-3).
detect(img, keypoints): standard public cv::Feature2D::detect overload; img is a valid non-empty cv::Mat, keypoints an output vector. No preconditions violated.
Memory ownership: AKAZE is returned as a cv::Ptr (refcounted); img is stack-owned and outlives the call; keypoints is caller-owned. No lifetime or ownership issues.

title: [Feature] Support medianBlur kernel sizes above 5 for images with more than four channels
body:
Problem
cv::medianBlur and cv2.medianBlur support images with more than four channels when ksize is 3 or 5. The same uint8 image is rejected when ksize is 7 or larger because the large-kernel path only accepts 1, 3, or 4 channels.
Changing only the kernel size should not change the set of supported channel counts. Multispectral images, feature maps, and stacked masks must currently be split into groups of at most four channels, filtered separately, and concatenated.
Minimal reproducer
import cv2
import numpy as np

for channels in (4, 5, 9):
    image = np.arange(
        17 * 19 * channels,
        dtype=np.uint8,
    ).reshape(17, 19, channels)

    for kernel_size in (3, 5, 7, 9):
        try:
            result = cv2.medianBlur(image, kernel_size)
            print(channels, kernel_size, result.shape)
        except cv2.error as error:
            print(
                channels,
                kernel_size,
                str(error).splitlines()[-1],
            )
Actual result
All channel counts work with kernel sizes 3 and 5. Kernel sizes 7 and 9 work for four channels but reject five and nine channels with:
src.depth() == CV_8U && (cn == 1 || cn == 3 || cn == 4)

Expected result
For every kernel size supported by the image depth, medianBlur should process any channel count supported by OpenCV and return the original (H, W, C) shape. Median filtering is channel-independent, so the fallback can process channels in groups internally if the optimized large-kernel implementation is specialized for 1, 3, and 4 channels.
Downstream impact
Albucore carries this exact fallback in its median_blur wrapper: kernel sizes 3 and 5 dispatch directly, while larger kernels split inputs above four channels into chunks. Native support would remove extra calls, concatenation, and temporary arrays.
Environment

OpenCV Python package: opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93
cv2.__version__: 5.0.0
Python: 3.12
NumPy: 2.2.6
Platform: macOS arm64

title: 5.x: IPP HAL warp functions ignore the cv::ipp::useIPP() runtime switch (missing CV_HAL_CHECK_USE_IPP)
body:
System Information
OpenCV version:    5.0.0 (also current 5.x, 172ea5a00c). 4.x is NOT affected.
IPP version:       2026.0.0 (bundled ippicv)
Operating System:  Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64
Compiler:          g++ 13.3.0
CMake:             4.2.0, default configuration with WITH_IPP=ON (the default)

Detailed description
(AI disclosure: Claude Fable-5 was used to diagnose and write up this issue after a manual library upgrade in a larger project caused unit tests to start failing. See #29279 for additional context.)
Commit 6bb3c31 ("Add useIPP check to hal_ipp functions") added CV_HAL_CHECK_USE_IPP() to every IPP HAL entry point so that the documented runtime switches — cv::ipp::setUseIPP(false) and the OPENCV_IPP=disabled environment variable — disable the IPP HAL as well as the legacy IPP paths.
On the 5.x branch, hal/ipp/src/warp_ipp.cpp is missing this check in all three of its entry points, while every other IPP HAL file has it:
$ grep -rn CV_HAL_CHECK_USE_IPP hal/ipp/src/
hal/ipp/src/cart_polar_ipp.cpp:12 / :25
hal/ipp/src/sum_ipp.cpp:14
hal/ipp/src/transforms_ipp.cpp:27 / :103
hal/ipp/src/mean_ipp.cpp:199
hal/ipp/src/norm_ipp.cpp:15 / :135
hal/ipp/src/minmax_ipp.cpp:163
        (no hits in warp_ipp.cpp: ipp_hal_warpAffine, ipp_hal_warpPerspective,
         ipp_hal_remap32f)

The 4.x branch has the check in warp_ipp.cpp; it appears to have been lost on 5.x in the warp rework (c2b8907, "rewoked warp perspective and aligned the whole file").
As a result, cv::ipp::setUseIPP(false) / OPENCV_IPP=disabled silently do nothing for warpAffine, warpPerspective, and remap on 5.x. This is not just cosmetic: IPP warpAffine INTER_NEAREST currently produces results that differ from the native implementation (#29279), and the broken switch removes the only runtime mitigation — the user is left with rebuilding OpenCV (WITH_IPP=OFF) or patching the dispatch table.
Suggested fix: add CV_HAL_CHECK_USE_IPP(); at the top of ipp_hal_warpAffine, ipp_hal_warpPerspective, and ipp_hal_remap32f in hal/ipp/src/warp_ipp.cpp, matching the 4.x branch.
Steps to reproduce
Inspection is sufficient (grep above), but the behavioral demonstration uses
the result mismatch from #29279 as the observable:
// g++ -O2 repro2.cpp -o repro2 $(pkg-config --cflags --libs opencv5)
// Run the #29279 reproducer body (16U vs 16S warp, angle 13.7) once
// with default settings and once after cv::ipp::setUseIPP(false). On 4.x
// (>= 6bb3c31450) the mismatch disappears after setUseIPP(false); on 5.x it
// is unchanged:
//
//   default:          454 of 810000 pixels differ
//   setUseIPP(false): 454 of 810000 pixels differ  ->  IPP still active
//
// (If #29279 gets fixed first, the equivalent check is to compare any
// IPP-dispatched warp result against a WITH_IPP=OFF build with
// setUseIPP(false) set — the outputs should be identical, and on 5.x are not
// guaranteed to be, because the IPP kernels still run.)
Expected: after cv::ipp::setUseIPP(false) (or with OPENCV_IPP=disabled in the environment), no IPP HAL code runs, matching the behavior of every other function in hal/ipp/ and of warp_ipp.cpp on 4.x.
Observed: the warp entry points dispatch to ipp::iwiWarpAffine / ippiWarpPerspective* / ippiRemap* regardless of the switch.

Detailed description
Summary
A heap buffer overflow (WRITE of size 4) occurs in the built-in MJPEG encoder's mjpeg_buffer::put_bits function when writing a frame whose dimensions cause the initial per-stripe buffer to be allocated with exactly 2 slots. When a put_bits call consumes exactly all remaining bits in the last slot (len == bits_free), the resize guard is not triggered, but the function unconditionally writes into the next (out-of-bounds) slot.
Version
$ git describe
4.13.0-150-gc7732e1043

Description
Buffer Allocation
When MjpegEncoder is constructed, each stripe's output buffer is sized as:
// cap_mjpeg_encoder.cpp:1200
m_buffer_list.allocate_buffers(stripes_count, (height * width * 2) / stripes_count);
For a 1×1 grayscale frame with stripes_count = 1, this yields (1 * 1 * 2) / 1 = 2 unsigned-int slots (8 bytes total).
Off-by-One in Resize Guard
The vulnerable function is put_bits (line 163–178):
// cap_mjpeg_encoder.cpp:163
inline void put_bits(unsigned bits, int len)
{
    CV_Assert(len >= 0 && len < 32);
    if ((m_pos == (data.size() - 1) && len > bits_free) || m_pos == data.size())
    {                                      // ^^^ BUG: should be >=
        resize(int(2 * data.size()));
    }

    bits_free -= (len);
    unsigned int tempval = (bits) & bit_mask[(len)];

    if (bits_free <= 0)
    {
        data[m_pos] |= ((unsigned)tempval >> -bits_free);
        bits_free += 32;
        ++m_pos;
        data[m_pos] = bits_free < 32 ? (tempval << bits_free) : 0;  // line 178: OOB WRITE
    }
    ...
}
The resize guard fires only when len > bits_free (strictly greater). When len == bits_free (the current slot is exactly filled), the guard is skipped. The code then enters the bits_free <= 0 branch, increments m_pos to data.size() (one past the end), and writes to data[m_pos] — a heap buffer overflow.

false → no resize

entered → ++m_pos; data[m_pos] = 0 → OOB WRITE



A len = 32 call is reachable because put_bits is called with cat values from the Huffman DC coefficient path (line 1334–1335), where cat can equal 0, and separately from put_val which can encode symbols requiring up to 16 bits; the combination through repeated encoding of DCT blocks on a 1×1 frame exhausts the buffer quickly.

title: core(opengl): memory leak in initializeContextFromGL() when clGetDeviceInfo fails
body:
System Information
OpenCV version: 4.x (latest, commit 9929b5c)
Operating System / Platform: N/A — identified via static code review
Compiler & compiler version: N/A
Detailed description
Memory leak in modules/core/src/opengl.cpp inside initializeContextFromGL().
A char[] buffer is heap-allocated to query OpenCL device extension strings.
If clGetDeviceInfo() returns a non-success status code, continue is executed, jumping past the delete[] that exists only on the success path. As a result, the allocated buffer is never freed.
The catch (...) block also does not release extensions, so exceptions thrown during allocation or OpenCL calls can leak the buffer as well.
Affected Lines
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.x/modules/core/src/opengl.cpp#L1688-L1692
extensions = new char[extensionSize];

status = clGetDeviceInfo(devices[j], CL_DEVICE_EXTENSIONS,
                         extensionSize, extensions, &extensionSize);

if (status != CL_SUCCESS)
    continue;  // `extensions` leaked here
Steps to reproduce
No runtime reproducer is required, as this is a static code defect.
The leak path is triggered when:

The application uses OpenCV with OpenCL + OpenGL interop enabled (HAVE_OPENCL_OPENGL_SHARING)
cv::ogl::ocl::initializeContextFromGL() is called
clGetDeviceInfo() returns any status other than CL_SUCCESS during the extension query

Affected Code
modules/core/src/opengl.cpp (around line 1685)
extensions = new char[extensionSize];  // allocated

status = clGetDeviceInfo(devices[j], CL_DEVICE_EXTENSIONS,
                         extensionSize, extensions, &extensionSize);

if (status != CL_SUCCESS)
    continue;  // `extensions` leaked  delete[] never reached
The continue statement bypasses the cleanup path, causing the allocated buffer to leak.

title: Python: add context manager compatibility for VideoCapture and VideoWriter
body:
Describe the feature and motivation
OpenCV video objects work like standard Python files in terms of error handling, where you have to close/release the file when you are done doing things with it if you don't want to have problems, even if errors interrupt the execution of the program. In Python, the standard way to do it is with a context manager, but this doesn't work with cv2.VideoCapture and cv2.VideoWriter objects.
Additional context
Let's say I have a video named video.avi in the same folder as the script I am running.
If I run this first script, everything works without any problem.
import cv2

file = "video.avi"

cap = cv2.VideoCapture(file)
ret, frame = cap.read()
cv2.imshow("Frame", frame)
cap.release()
If I run this script instead, I cannot rename the video from the File Explorer afterwards, as it is already open in Python, until I restart the kernel.
import cv2

file = "video.avi"

cap = cv2.VideoCapture(file)
ret, frame = cap.read()
cv2.imshow("Frame", frame)
# Do a bunch of things that cause an error
raise RuntimeError
cap.release()
If instead I try to use a context manager to open the video, which would release it at the end no matter whether there is an error or not, I get an error message : TypeError: 'cv2.VideoCapture' object does not support the context manager protocol (missed __exit__ method)
import cv2

file = "video.avi"

with cv2.VideoCapture(file) as cap:
    ret, frame = cap.read()
    cv2.imshow("Frame", frame)

title: VideoCap image sequences cannot start beyond backend's auto-probe window
body:
Describe the feature and motivation
Neither CAP_IMAGES nor CAP_FFMPEG exposes a way to specify where the sequence begins when using printf style patterns to read image sequences.
Both fall back to a built-in probe, and any sequences outside that window wont open.
CAP_IMAGES only tries frames 0 and 1 then gives up.
CAP_FFMPEG defaults to 0 and ranges up to 5 (0 to 4).
Aside from sequences which might start at a higher number I think it should be possible to specify what the start of the sequence is regardless, so my suggestion would be a CAP_PROP_IMAGE_SEQ_START as an open only property that sets the first frame index when a VideoCapture is opened with this printf sequence pattern.
CAP_IMAGES doesn't currently have a variant with params so that would need to be added.
I will submit a PR shortly with my suggestion for an implementation of this.

title: Resource leaks in Android Utils.java exportResource() and loadResource()
body: In Utils.java, exportResource() opens InputStream and FileOutputStream without try-with-resources. If IOException occurs during read/write, streams are never closed. Same pattern in loadResource(). On Android, leaked file descriptors can exhaust the process fd limit. Fix: convert to try-with-resources.

title: HighGui.java: System.exit(-1) in library code should throw exceptions instead
body: HighGui.java calls System.exit(-1) in 3 places (imshow with empty image, waitKey without prior imshow, waitKey with null image). Library code should never call System.exit() as it kills the entire JVM. Should throw IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException instead. Also has printStackTrace() in InterruptedException catch block.

I found an UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (UBSan) error in OpenCV's count non-zero operations. The bug occurs when calling cv::countNonZero() on 32-bit float matrices, where the function cv::opt_AVX2::countNonZero32f is called through a pointer with an incorrect function type.
Description
The root cause of this bug is a function pointer type mismatch in the countNonZero dispatch mechanism.
In modules/core/src/count_non_zero.dispatch.cpp, the getCountNonZeroTab() function returns a table of function pointers cast to CountNonZeroFunc type. The CountNonZeroFunc typedef is defined as:
typedef int (*CountNonZeroFunc)(const uchar*, int);

int countNonZero32f(const float* src, int len);

Detailed description
cv::error with cv::breakOnError set to true, as implemented in system.cpp L.1283 causes undefined behaviour (UB) by dereferencing nullptr to, I suppose, cause a SEGFAULT and crash the programme.
There is no guarantee as per the C++ Standard (nor the C Standard, for that matters) that this will cause a SEGFAULT. In fact, smart compilers will diagnose and recognise this assignment to nullptr and may not generate code for it, as it's allowed by the Standard.
I am aware this is a really old piece of code (!), yet I believe this is still a relevant thing to fix.
The "idiomatic" C++ way would be to call std::terminate (C++11) instead, which will also call any std::terminate_handler installed by the user or other libraries, if any, or std::abort which will SIGARBT without UB.
Note that dereferencing nullptr is also a security vulnerability any way (if it causes a SEGFAULT), as it can generate a core dump that can potentially leak sensitive information an unprivileged user could access (in some restricted circumstances, of course).

title: [DNN/ONNX] Squeeze operator fails when axes is empty
body:
System Information

OpenCV Version: 4.13.0
OS: Linux
Python: 3.10
ONNX Opset: 11
Comparison: ONNX Runtime (works correctly)

Detailed description
OpenCV's DNN module incorrectly handles the ONNX Squeeze operator when all axes are squeezed (i.e., removing all dimensions of size 1). While ONNX Runtime correctly produces a [64, 64] output tensor, OpenCV DNN retains the original [1, 1, 64, 64] shape.
Expected Behavior
When a Squeeze node removes all size-1 dimensions:

Input shape: [1, 1, 64, 64]
Expected output: [64, 64]

Actual Behavior (OpenCV DNN)

Actual output: [1, 1, 64, 64] (no dimensions removed)

ONNX Runtime Behavior (Reference)

Output: [64, 64] ✓ (correct)

Steps to reproduce
Steps to Reproduce
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import cv2
import onnxruntime as ort

class SqueezeAllDims(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return torch.squeeze(x)  # Remove all size-1 dims

model = SqueezeAllDims()
model.eval()

input_tensor = torch.randn(1, 1, 64, 64)

# Export to ONNX
torch.onnx.export(model, input_tensor, "squeeze_bug.onnx",
                 input_names=['input'], output_names=['output'],
                 opset_version=11)

# ONNX Runtime (correct)
ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("squeeze_bug.onnx")
ort_out = ort_session.run(None, {'input': input_tensor.numpy()})[0]
print(f"ONNX Runtime shape: {ort_out.shape}")  # (64, 64) ✓

# OpenCV DNN (bug)
net = cv2.dnn.readNetFromONNX("squeeze_bug.onnx")
net.setInput(input_tensor.numpy())
cv_out = net.forward()
print(f"OpenCV DNN shape: {cv_out.shape}")  # (1, 1, 64, 64) ✗
Analysis
The issue likely stems from the Squeeze layer implementation in OpenCV DNN:

File: modules/dnn/src/layers/reshape_layer.cpp (SqueezeLayer)
Root cause: When the axes attribute is empty or not specified, the layer should squeeze all dimensions of size 1, but OpenCV appears to skip this operation

ONNX Specification
According to ONNX Squeeze operator spec:

If axes is not provided, all the single dimensions will be removed from the shape.

OpenCV DNN does not correctly implement this fallback behavior.
Proposed Fix
In modules/dnn/src/layers/reshape_layer.cpp, the Squeeze layer should:

Check if axes parameter is empty
If empty, automatically detect and remove all dimensions where size == 1
Update output shape accordingly

Example pseudocode:
if (axes.empty()) {
    // Squeeze ALL dimensions of size 1
    for (int i = 0; i < input_shape.size(); i++) {
        if (input_shape[i] != 1) {
            output_shape.push_back(input_shape[i]);
        }
    }
} else {
    // Squeeze only specified axes
    // ... existing logic ...
}
Attachments

ONNX file: squeeze_bug.onnx.zip
squeeze_bug.onnx.zip

Impact
This affects any model using torch.squeeze() without axis specification, including:

Models with dynamic batch sizes normalized to 1
Auto-encoder bottleneck layers
Channel-wise global pooling outputs

body:
System Information
OpenCV version: 4.x (current master)
Operating System / Platform: macOS
Compiler & compiler version: Apple Clang (Xcode default)
Detailed description
BmpDecoder::readData and SunRasterDecoder::readData compute src_pitch
using width × bits-per-pixel arithmetic without sufficient overflow checks.
For large crafted image widths, these calculations can overflow 32-bit
integers, resulting in insufficient buffer allocation. Subsequent decoding
logic (e.g. row copy operations) may then read beyond the allocated buffer,
causing a heap buffer over-read.
Affected code

modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_bmp.cpp
modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_sunras.cpp

Impact
A malformed BMP or SunRaster image may trigger out-of-bounds memory access
during decoding via cv::imdecode.
Root cause

Missing overflow checks for width × bpp calculations
Missing bounds checks for width × channel count

Steps to reproduce
Reproduction
The issue can be triggered by decoding a crafted BMP or SunRaster image
with very large width values that cause width × bpp arithmetic to overflow.
Example parameters:

Width: 134217731
Height: 1
Bits per pixel: 32

When decoded, the computed src_pitch overflows and results in insufficient
buffer allocation.
A minimal reproducer can be constructed by crafting an image header with
the above values and passing it to cv::imdecode.
Issue submission checklist

 I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, forum.opencv.org, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found any solution
 I updated to the latest OpenCV version and the issue is still there
 There is reproducer code and related data files (videos, images, onnx, etc)

title: Mac Catalyst build fails with clang error "-mllvm is not supported with -fembed-bitcode"
body:
System Information

OpenCV: 4.13.0
Xcode: 15.2
Target: Mac Catalyst (arm64, x86_64)
Build system: platforms/apple/build_xcframework.py

Detailed description
Building OpenCV for Mac Catalyst using the official build scripts fails with Apple Clang:
clang: error: -mllvm is not supported with -fembed-bitcode

This happens when compiling the kleidicv_neon target.

Steps to reproduce
Using the standard xcframework build script:
python3 platforms/apple/build_xcframework.py \
    --iphoneos_archs=arm64 \
    --visionos_archs=arm64 \
    --visionsimulator_archs=arm64 \
    --disable-bitcode \
    -o build
During the Catalyst build phase, the following is executed internally:
python3 platforms/osx/build_framework.py build/catalyst \
    --catalyst_archs x86_64,arm64 \
    --framework_name opencv2 \
    --build_only_specified_archs \
    --disable-bitcode

The script reports:
The following args are not recognized and will not be used: ['--disable-bitcode']


Observed behavior
The Catalyst build eventually fails with:
clang: error: -mllvm is not supported with -fembed-bitcode

title: `cv::Mat_<T>::copyTo` can no longer be used on empty matrices
body:
System Information
After updating to OpenCV 4.13.0 one of my unit tests started failing with an OpenCV exception while trying to invoke copyTo on empty matrices of fixed type. In general, copyTo on empty matrices should be a no op and always succeed.
Bisecting the issue points to 64bbaa9 (#27972) as the commit that introduced the regression.
Detailed description
cv::Mat::copyTo can no longer be invoked on empty matrices of fixed type. Trying to do so fails with the following exception:
OpenCV(4.13.0) Error: Assertion failed (!fixedType() || ((Mat*)obj)->type() == mtype) in create, file /home/sergiu/Projects/opencv/modules/core/src/matrix_wrap.cpp, line 1321
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'cv::Exception'
  what():  OpenCV(4.13.0) /home/sergiu/Projects/opencv/modules/core/src/matrix_wrap.cpp:1321: error: (-215:Assertion failed) !fixedType() || ((Mat*)obj)->type() == mtype in function 'create'
Steps to reproduce
#include <opencv2/core.hpp>

int main()
{
    cv::Mat_<double> a;
    cv::Mat_<double> b;
    a.copyTo(b);
}

title: The description of `universal intrinsics` deviates from the current implementation.
body:
Describe the doc issue
There are not enough SIMD techniques mentioned in the documentation compared to the currently implemented SIMD techniques.
https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/dd1/tutorial_univ_intrin.html
https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/df/d91/group__core__hal__intrin.html
Fix suggestion

use v_add() function instead of C++ operator (It seems be impportant information).
Add a list of supported SIMD technologies to the API documentation (to avoid duplication with the tutorial comments).
Expand the list of supported SIMD technologies.
Mention VLA related to RVV 1.0/SVE.
